reason: Lens 4 (counterexamples and logic). Every refutation filed against step 3 (team games via 104.2c, Archenemy via 103.1b, draw overlap via 104.4a, simultaneous first losers via 704.3, Supervillain Rumble via 904.12c, win-by-effect with no stated losers, and a player who drew under 104.4e/801.16 being deemed a loser) was answered by a fix in the rule's own text, and the final report passed with no standing refutation. I re-ran each counterexample against the final wording. Team, Archenemy and Supervillain Rumble games are excluded. Any game that was a draw, for the whole game or for any one player, goes by the 103.1 draw sentence. Simultaneous first losers have a stated tie-break. Players still in the game when a winner wins by an effect count as losers at that moment. Because the rule requires one winner and that no player left with a draw, every game it reaches has a determinate first loser or a determinate tied set, and 103.1 gives no competing answer. 800.4h does not apply, since the 103.1 chooser acts at the start of the next game, as a player of that game. 103.1 says only 'the loser', so it is silent when there are several losers; the stipulation fills that gap and contradicts no cited CR text. Steps 1, 2 and 4 are sourced and claim no more than their quotes. Step 3 is a stipulation I accept as the rule. Residual points are not refutations: 'cannot agree' is undefined, and limited-range-of-influence wins that do not end the game are not spelled out.

evidence.excerpt: In a match of several games, the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn.
If the previous game was a draw, the player who made the choice in that game makes the choice in this game.
If the game is a draw for a player, that player leaves the game.
Rather, the archenemy takes the first turn.
Each player on the winning team wins the game, even if one or more of those players had previously lost that game.
